question.text: When SIAB considers an allegation of professional misconduct against an SIA who has a prior warning / censure on record for a similar default, the repeat element typically:

answer.text: Results in automatic debarment without hearing - hearing is waived for repeat offenders.
Triggers a compulsory three-year debarment irrespective of severity.
Is ignored - each proceeding starts de novo with no reference to past record.
Is treated as an aggravating factor in determining sanction, moving the proceeding toward suspension / cancellation rather than warning / censure.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** In disciplinary jurisprudence, a prior record of similar misconduct is an aggravating factor guiding sanction choice. SIAB, mirroring ICAI Council practice, moves from the lower end of the sanction menu (warning, censure) to the higher end (suspension, cancellation, debarment) when repeat conduct is established. Hearing is not waived; the principles of natural justice still apply. **The Trap:** Automatic debarment without hearing (A), ignoring past record (C), and compulsory fixed debarment (D) each over- or under-shoot the calibrated approach. **Cross-Exam Context:** III-A/III-C tests repeat-offender sanction escalation for compliance officers; XXIII tests the same philosophy for SIAs. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** If acting as counsel for a SIA with a prior record, front-load remediation evidence: additional CPE credits, peer-review sign-off on later engagements, voluntary compliance attestations. These evidence-based remediation facts materially soften the sanction.
